newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: DOWNER PLAYING DOWN PLUTONIUM SHIPMENT
Reports a proposed shipment of plutonium could pass through the Tasman Sea have raised concerns in New Zealand.
But Australia's foreign minister Alexander Downer says he's taking a wait-and-see attitude on the matter.
Greenpeace says a leaked French Government document outlines plans of the proposed shipment.
Mr Downer says it's too early to voice any concerns and he'll wait until the final route of the shipment is known.
The New Zealand Foreign Minister, Don McKinnon, has already asked Japan for assurances the shipment will not enter his country's exclusive economic zone.
KENNETT WARNS GOVT ON CAR INDUSTRY
The Federal Government has been warned Australia's car industry will be destroyed if a report is accepted to slash tariffs to 5 percent.
Victoria's Premier, Jeff Kennett, says hundreds of thousands of jobs will go if a majority report by the Industry Commission is accepted.
The report, commissioned by the Federal Government, has recommended tariffs protecting local car makers, be cut to 5 per cent by the year 2004.
Mr Kennett has questioned the claim that consumers are paying close to 4,000 more for cars, because of tariffs.
He says he doesn't accept that figure, or the ramifications of the report unchallenged.
REVIEW OF SOCIAL SECURITY APPEAL SYSTEM ANNOUNCED
Social Security Minister, Jocelyn Newman's announced a review of the Social Security appeals system.
Former Liberal Senator Dame Margaret Guilfoyle will do the review.
Senator Newman says the review will look at the operation of the social security appeals tribunal including its powers and membership arrangements.
Dame Margaret will provide an interim report by April next year.
WOOLIES TO BAN POLYSTYRENE PACKAGING
Retailer Woolworths says that its buyers won't accept a type of polystyrene packaging from fruit and vegetable growers from next month.
It will force growers to move to cardboard packaging for such things as broccoli, stone fruit, tomatoes and grapes.
Woolworths say it has a problem disposing of the used polystyrene boxes.
The Plastics and Chemicals Industries Association say that it had made Woolworths an offer, worth about four-million dollars, to collect the unwanted boxes from supermarkets.
Paul McGuigan of the Farmers' Federation, says that Woolworths isn't the only retailer whose produce buyers won't accept polystyrene:
GARIBALDI DIRECTORS GRANTED STAY
In Adelaide, three former directors of the collapsed Garibaldi Smallgoods company, facing manslaughter charges, have been granted a stay of criminal proceedings.
Luciano Marchi, his son Philip and the former company's financial controller Neville Mead are charged over the death of a four-year-old girl last year.
The three men had told the Supreme Court they couldn't afford their defence bill, likely to be more than 300-thousand dollars.
NEW RUNS PROPOSED FOR MT HOTHAM
A hearing is underway into a proposal for two new ski runs at Mt Hotham.
Planning Minister Rob MacLellan called-in applications for the ski field expansion, and for a proposed airport at Horsehair Plain, south of Mount Hotham.
The hearing's due to finish next week, and Minister MacLellan expects to make a decision by mid-January.
The Victorian National Parks Association objects to the proposal, saying it pre-empts a statewide alpine resort plan.
